summary: Version tracking and release notes are now visible in the app.
details: Added a version number to the footer
Added a "What's new" panel to the left nav with full changelog history

summary: Minor Improvements the release notes panel
details: Some minor UI improvements to the release notes panel

summary: Added a new Companies and Locations system.
details: Added a "Location" option to the login portal.
Added custom theme customisation for each company.
Added the ability to upload a logo to show in the sidebar when logged in.
Fixed the "What's New" panel not ordering the changelog correctly.
Added some UI improvements to the Role and User Role Managment pages.

summary: Major Performance improvements.
details: Added a fix for a bug that would cause a loading spinner to show for 5 seconds when loading any page.
Added a fix for a bug that would cause the Companies logo to be hidden on the sidebar in the mobile view

summary: Added a new Help system.
details: Added a new Help panel accessible from areas that have help documents available.
Users with the "Manager" role can now open the User and Role Management pages.
Users with the "Manager" role can now bulk-assign training courses.

summary: Updated site branding.
details: Updated the site to use the specific Lanyard logos for the browser icon.

summary: Added rich interactions to the File Manager Page.
details: Added Folder Creation to the File Manager Page.
Added the ability to move files in the File Manager Page.
Added the ability to download files in the File Manager Page.

summary: Added the "CanManageFiles" role.
details: Added a new role "CanManageFiles" that allows users to manage files and folders in the File Manager Page.
Added a rate limit of 25 requests per minute for endpoints that are related to logging in and logging out.
Added a small UI improvement to the "My Training" card on the home page
Added UI updates to the Bulk Assign Course dialog to make it more user friendly.
Added the Company logo to the home page on the mobile interface.

summary: Managers can now create users, plus training history and file manager improvements.
details: Managers can now create, delete, and resend invites for users, matching Admin permissions.
The new-password invite email now shows the location to log in at.
Added a confirmation dialog before deleting a file in the File Manager.
Added the ability to edit a user's name, phone number, and date of birth on the Users page.
The company logo area in the side navbar is now hidden when no logo is set.
My Training and the manager's per-course and per-person training views now collapse multiple attempts into one row per course, expandable to see each attempt's score and result.
The kiosk text widget now supports rich text formatting (bold, italic, underline, lists).
Added 2fa support into the login system, enabled via the Account Managment Page

summary: Added email reminders for training assignments.
details: Users are now emailed when a training course is assigned to them.
Users are now emailed a reminder when an assigned course's due date is within 7 days and still incomplete.

summary: Login page overhaul with a company picker and optional background image.
details: Login now starts with a company-selection step before showing the username/password/location form, scoped to that company's locations.
Admins can set an optional login background image per company from the Companies and Locations page.
The login page's accent color now follows the selected company's brand color, and persists across a page refresh.
The mobile bottom navigation bar no longer shows on the login page until signed in.
Fixed the "Lanyard" wordmark rendering incorrectly on mobile browsers.
Fixed the login background not filling the full page height and an unwanted scrollbar on some screen sizes.

summary: Fixed slow volume dragging, a slow kiosk startup countdown, and made the Music page phone-friendly.
details: Fixed the volume slider on the Music page taking up to 20 seconds to reach the client after a drag - it now applies the change as soon as you release the slider.
Fixed the kiosk client's startup countdown taking around 20 seconds instead of the 5 seconds it displays.
The Music page now switches to a Playlists/Songs tab view on phone-sized screens instead of squeezing both side by side.
Added a Projection Control page showing every projection program currently running, which client and display it is on, and which step it is showing.
Projection programs can now be paused, resumed, stepped forwards or backwards, and stopped while they are playing.
A projection program triggered on a client now closes itself and returns the display to its normal programme once it has finished, instead of leaving its last step on screen.
The kiosk debug overlay now shows the current step and whether playback is paused.
Added a Kiosk Health dashboard widget listing every kiosk, offline ones first, with an online count and a "last seen" time for anything that has dropped.
The Kiosk Health widget can be set to show only offline kiosks, for a problems-only dashboard.
Kiosks now record when they disconnect, so downtime can be shown rather than just a bare online/offline state.
The Clients management page now refreshes on its own, so a kiosk going offline no longer needs a manual page reload to show up.
Logging out now goes straight to the login page instead of briefly showing an error screen on the way.
Passing a training course now emails you a branded PDF certificate automatically.
Added a "Download Certificate" button to the course completion dialog and to each completed course on My Training.
Certificates carry your company's logo and brand colour, and can be re-downloaded at any time.
Training emails now greet you by first name instead of your username.
Training emails and certificates now take their logo and brand colour from your own company, so everyone at a company gets consistent branding regardless of who assigned the course.

summary: Set a Dashboard as your Home Screen, Game results are now saved, with a Hall of Fame leaderboard widget and idle-triggered automation rules.
details: Finished laser games are now recorded, so scores survive a server restart instead of being lost the moment the next game starts.
Added a Hall of Fame dashboard widget showing top scores, best accuracy and team totals over Today, This Week, This Month or All Time.
The Hall of Fame widget can be pointed at a single kiosk or left venue-wide, and each section can be turned on or off.

Fixed player accuracy and team not updating during a game - both were frozen at whatever the first score packet of the game reported, so accuracy read far lower than it should have on the live scoreboard.
Automation rules can now be triggered by a kiosk sitting idle for a set number of minutes, not just by a game starting or ending.
Added a "Stop Projection Program" automation action that stops what is playing on a display and closes the window, so a screen can be cleared when a game starts.
Leaderboard periods reset at local midnight, so a screen running late into the evening rolls over at the right time.
You can now choose any dashboard as your home screen, so it shows instead of the standard home page when you open Lanyard.
Set it from the new Home Screen section on the Account Management page, or straight from the home icon next to any dashboard on the Dashboards page.
Dashboard widgets stay fully interactive on the home screen - buttons, playlist selectors and music controls all work without opening the dashboard.
Clicking the home icon on the dashboard that is already your home screen clears it, putting the standard home page back.
If a dashboard set as someone's home screen is later deleted, they are shown the standard home page again with a note explaining why, rather than a broken or empty screen.
Dashboards now stack into a single readable column on phone-sized screens instead of squeezing every widget into twelve narrow columns.
Fixed the Users page only ever showing the first 10 users, with no page controls to reach the others - it now shows 25 per page with working first/previous/next/last buttons and a total count.
Searching the Users page now jumps back to the first page of results instead of leaving you on an empty page.
Fixed the same problem on the Projection Programs and Projection Templates pages, where anything past the 10th program or template was hidden.

summary: Added a My Training dashboard widget, Added a way for admins and managers to set a home screen for everyone.
details: Added a "My Training" dashboard widget listing your own outstanding courses with their due date and status, overdue ones first.
The My Training widget shows each person their own training, so one shared dashboard works for the whole team.
Clicking a course in the My Training widget takes you straight to it.
The My Training widget can be set to include completed courses, and to cap how many courses it lists.
Courses in the My Training widget are now separated by a divider line with the course name emphasised, so a list of several courses no longer reads as one block of text.
The Users page table can now be sorted by Username, Name, Email Address or Status by clicking a column heading.
The Users page now shows 15 users per page instead of 25.
Editing, deleting or inviting a user no longer sends you back to the first page of the user list.
Admins and managers can set a dashboard as the home screen for everyone, from the new "Everyone's Home Screen" column on the Dashboards page.
Staff who have not picked a home screen of their own now see that dashboard when they open Lanyard, instead of the standard home page.
Setting or clearing everyone's home screen asks for confirmation first, since it changes what the whole team sees.
Anyone who has chosen their own home screen dashboard keeps it - a personal choice always wins over the organisation-wide one.
Added a "Follow the organisation default" option to the Home Screen section on the Account Management page, alongside "Use the standard home page" for anyone who would rather opt out entirely.
If the dashboard set as everyone's home screen is later deleted, staff see the standard home page again with a note explaining why, rather than an empty screen.
Added a Greeting dashboard widget showing the same "Good morning / afternoon / evening" card as the standard home page, with your name.
Added the name of your current location to the footer, so it is clear at a glance which site you are signed in to. This shows on desktop, where the footer bar is visible.
Fixed the "By Person" tab on the Training Dashboard listing every person in the system, so a manager could open the training record of someone at a different location.
The person picker now lists only people at your location, matching the By Course, Timing and Analytics tabs and the bulk assign dialog.
If someone belongs to more than one location, their record now shows only the training assigned at your location.
The deleted-user placeholder no longer appears as a selectable person in the picker.
Fixed the Training Courses page ignoring the location an Admin picked at login - it listed every course from every location, so signing in to one venue looked identical to signing in to another.
Admins now see only the courses belonging to the location they signed in to, plus any shared with it, the same view a Manager gets.
Added a "Show all locations" switch on the Training Courses page so an Admin can still review every location's courses in one list, with a banner making it clear when that is on.
Added a Location column to the Training Courses list, so it is obvious which venue each course belongs to and which courses have no location set at all.
A course created by an admin is now filed under the location they are signed in to, instead of having no location and disappearing from the list it was created on.
The current location now also shows in the header on phone-sized screens, where the footer that normally shows it is hidden.

summary: Admins and managers can now unlock a locked-out user account.
details: Fixed a bug where a login error - such as a locked account, invalid credentials, or a location access error - was not shown, and instead sent the user back to the company selection screen with no explanation.
Login errors are now shown on the login screen where they belong.
Added an unlock icon on the Users page for any account temporarily locked out from too many failed sign-in attempts, so staff no longer have to wait out the lockout timer.
The Users page Status column now shows "Locked" for an account currently locked out.

summary: Tidied up the Training Dashboard's Analytics tab.
details: Fixed the charts on the Training Dashboard's Analytics tab being cut off - a course with a lot of trainees ran off the bottom of its card and over the card below it.
The Analytics cards now all line up at the same height, and grow as tall as they need to so every trainee in a list is visible.
Removed the "Slowest Completions" chart, which on most courses just repeated "Fastest Completions" in the opposite order.

summary: Added Staff Announcements, with a dashboard widget to show them. Added a Projection Status dashboard widget showing live "now playing" progress.
details: Added an Announcements page where managers can post notices for their location - give someone the new "CanPostAnnouncements" role on the Roles page to let them write announcements.
An announcement can be pinned so it always shows at the top, and given an expiry date so it disappears on its own once it's no longer relevant.
Added an Announcements dashboard widget showing the live announcements for your location. Right-click it while editing a dashboard to choose how many to show.
Added a "Projection Status" dashboard widget that shows what's currently playing on a client's display, live, with the program name and a step-by-step progress bar.
The widget updates instantly as playback advances, pauses or is skipped, with no page refresh needed.
The widget can optionally show pause, resume, previous, next and stop controls, so it can be used read-only on a public kiosk dashboard, or with controls on a staff one.
Automation rules can now use a "Projection Program Control" action to start, stop, pause, resume, or skip to the next or previous step of a projection program on a client's display.

Added Pause, Resume, Skip and Stop actions to dashboard Button widgets, alongside the existing Trigger action, so a button can control whatever projection program is already playing rather than only starting a new one.
The Skip button action can be set to skip to either the next or the previous step.
These new button actions are Admin/Manager-only, matching the existing projection trigger button.

summary: Fixed kiosk command reliability, scoped employee lists to location, made the Training and User Management pages phone-friendly, and added DMX fixture/scene previews.
details: Fixed Play, Pause, Seek, volume, and song-change commands sometimes taking several seconds to reach a kiosk, getting slower the longer the kiosk had been running.
Fixed the kiosk occasionally losing its connection to the server and not automatically reconnecting.
Fixed the laser game status widget sometimes getting stuck showing a finished game's countdown timer instead of clearing when the game ends.
Fixed laser game starts sometimes being detected a moment later than they actually happened.
Fixed an issue where reloading a dashboard mid-song (for example after a mobile browser reconnects) could cause an unwanted jump in playback.
The Users page, Staff Roles page, and Training assignment screens now only show employees at your own location, instead of everyone across every site.
Everyone, including Admins, now picks a location when signing in - this was previously optional for Admins.

The Course Editor's section/quiz-question editor now switches to a single full-width view with a Back button on a phone, instead of an unusable side-by-side split that used to squeeze the editor into a sliver of the screen.
The Course Editor's details form now uses the full screen width on a phone instead of a narrow column.
The Training Dashboard and Training Help tabs now scroll sideways on a phone instead of cutting off tabs past "By Person"/"Creating Courses".
The My Training, Training Dashboard and Training Courses lists now scroll sideways on a phone instead of clipping course names and status badges off the edge of the screen.
Buttons and switches in the Training Courses header now wrap onto a second line on a phone instead of overlapping.
Tapping a user row now opens a dialog with all of that user's actions (edit, change password, resend invite, unlock, delete, etc.) instead of a row of small icons.
The Username and Email columns now hide on narrow screens to keep the table readable on a phone.
Added a Fixtures manager to the DMX desk, so staff can define a client's rig once (name, starting channel, and Dimmer / RGB / RGB + Dimmer type).
Added a Fixture Preview mode to the DMX desk that renders defined fixtures as colored lights instead of raw channel sliders, updating live as channels change.
Added a Preview Scene button to the scene editor that animates a scene through its steps entirely in the browser, with a play/pause control and a scrubber to jump straight to any step.

summary: Fixed the file/folder list API silently failing, and training courses being auto-assigned to new users regardless of location.
details: Fixed the file and folder listing endpoints returning a success response even when the underlying request failed, which could show an empty or stale file list instead of a clear error.

Courses marked to auto-assign on user creation now only assign to a new user if the course belongs to one of the user's own locations, or is shared with the company that location belongs to - previously it assigned every such course to every new user across all locations.

summary: Added staff document tracking with expiry reminders, automated onboarding emails, a redesigned user profile page, plus Music, File Manager, and training course fixes.
details: Added a Documents tab to each staff member's profile, where documents like DBS checks, First Aid certificates and other paperwork can be uploaded, tracked and downloaded.
Admins and managers can define their own catalog of document types under Manage > Staff Document Types, including whether a type requires an expiry date.
Staff members are emailed automatically when one of their documents is approaching its expiry date, with reminder timing configurable per document type (e.g. 30 and 7 days before expiry).

Clicking a user in Manage > Users now opens a dedicated page instead of a popup dialog, giving the Details, Password, Account, Documents and Danger Zone tabs more room to breathe. The page can be linked to directly and works with the browser's back/forward buttons.

Removing a song from a playlist on the Music page now keeps it off the list - previously it could reappear a moment later (e.g. while a song was playing) and clicking Remove again would fail with "Song is not in this playlist".
The File Manager's Size column now shows file sizes as B/KB/MB/GB instead of a raw byte count.
Fixed the song list on the Music page silently clipping songs instead of scrolling once the list grew taller than the available space, on both desktop and mobile layouts.
Added a new Manage > Onboarding page where admins can turn on an automatic welcome email for newly created users, with a custom subject and rich-text body.
Admins can curate a standing set of files (handbook, starter forms, posters) that are automatically attached to every onboarding welcome email for their company.
The welcome email is sent automatically the moment a new user account is created, and never blocks account creation if it fails to send.
Managers can now view and edit the Onboarding settings too, not just Admins - scoped to only the companies and locations they actually belong to.
Onboarding settings can now be configured per location instead of only company-wide, with a toggle to switch between the two - a location without its own override falls back to the company default.
Adding a standing attachment now opens a dialog instead of showing a permanently-visible upload area on the page.
Fixed bullet-point lists in course section content turning into numbered lists when previewed or completed by a learner, even though they showed correctly while being edited.
A new standing attachment can now be uploaded directly from the Add Attachment dialog, instead of needing a separate trip to the File Manager first.
Fixed the onboarding welcome email's rich-text toolbar being unreadable in dark mode.
Managers can now open Manage > Staff Document Types too, not just Admins - scoped to only their own company, matching the same access Managers already have to Onboarding settings.
Added a Staff Document Types link to the Manage nav menu, which was previously missing even for Admins.

Fixed the Staff Document Types list rendering as a fixed-column table, which squashed the reminder-days input taller than its own row and clipped long names on a phone - it's now a plain list that wraps and resizes properly on any screen.

summary: Staff document reminders are now set per document instead of per document type, bulk onboarding attachments, a stuck File Manager delete fix, a fix for the Onboarding settings page not showing a location's saved configuration, and admins can now customize a new user's welcome email at the point of registration.
details: Removed the reminder-days configuration from Staff Document Types - document types no longer have a reminder policy of their own.
When uploading a document to a staff member, the uploader now sets a custom expiry date and reminder date for that specific document.
The staff member's Documents tab now shows the configured reminder date alongside the expiry date.
Documents uploaded before this change won't have a reminder date until they're re-uploaded.

The Add Attachment dialog on the Onboarding settings page now supports adding several documents in one session - drag/drop or select multiple files at once, or add multiple existing files from the library, without the dialog closing after each one.
Selecting or dropping more files than allowed now shows a clear message instead of crashing the page.

Fixed a bug where removing a standing attachment from the Onboarding settings page permanently blocked that file from being deleted in the File Manager, even though it was no longer attached to anything.

The Onboarding settings page now correctly detects and shows a location's saved welcome email settings on load, instead of looking blank when only a location-specific configuration (and no company-wide one) had been saved.
Fixed saving Onboarding settings crashing with an error after turning "Configure separately per location" on and back off.
The Register New User dialog now shows a "Customize welcome email for this user" option once a location is selected, prefilled with that location's default subject and rich-text body.
Editing the subject or body only changes the email sent to that one new user - the shared company/location welcome email template is left untouched.
The option is disabled with an explanatory message if welcome emails aren't enabled for the selected location.

summary: Performance and reliability improvements across staff pages, kiosks, DMX lighting, music and file streaming.
details: Moving the mouse or scrolling no longer sends a constant stream of activity pings to the server - the auto-logout timer now hears from the browser at most once every few seconds.

File downloads, music streaming, image thumbnails, company logos and training certificates are no longer subject to the 25-requests-per-minute login rate limit, which had been shared by every kiosk and staff device behind a venue's network and could return "Too many requests" for large image folders or kiosks warming their song cache.

Kiosk dashboard steps no longer reload the dashboard from the database every time the kiosk screen refreshes (including on every pause/resume) - only when the step actually switches to a different dashboard.
The kiosk page no longer renders every widget twice on each program step.
The clock-in screen's second-by-second timers are now properly stopped when you leave the page instead of running in the background for the rest of your session.
Fixed a rare freeze of music playback control for all kiosks caused by the shuffle picker using a shared random-number generator from several places at once.
Playing a single song no longer performs a pointless playlist lookup, and the music player's database connections are released promptly.
The DMX scene list no longer loads every step of every scene just to show a step count.
The server no longer writes every SQL statement to the log, which was the single largest source of log volume in production.

Each DMX scene step now reaches the kiosk as a single message carrying every channel in the step, instead of one message per channel. Pushing the whole virtual desk live is likewise one message rather than 512.
The kiosk no longer echoes every channel value it receives back to the server, which had been doubling all DMX traffic and server work.
The virtual DMX desk now redraws at most about twenty times a second while a scene is running or a fader is dragged, instead of once per channel change, so it stays responsive during playback.
Scene steps no longer smear out over time as the channels are sent one after another - all channels in a step land together.
A scene running for a kiosk that is offline no longer queries the database on every step.
Kiosk client 1.0.40 is required: a kiosk still running an older client will not respond to DMX scenes or the virtual desk until it auto-updates on its next restart.

Kiosk "Play a Video" steps now stream the video straight from storage. Previously the server loaded the entire file into memory and pushed it to the kiosk screen as inline text on every step, which for a large video meant hundreds of megabytes of work per step per kiosk.
Seeking or looping in a video or song no longer re-downloads the whole file: the server now asks storage for just the bytes the player requests.
File downloads, music and kiosk videos are now cacheable by the browser for a day, so thumbnails and repeated plays don't re-fetch the same bytes.
The File Manager, file pickers and image grid now show only the files and folders that actually live in the selected folder. The root folder used to list every file in every folder.
The image picker no longer reloads its folder (and flashes its spinner) every time the surrounding page re-renders.
The server now shares one storage connection for all file operations instead of creating a new one per page and request, and releases its database connections promptly after every file operation.
The server no longer writes every SQL statement to the log, which was the single largest source of log volume in production.
The login company picker and the sign-in form no longer reload (and briefly blank out) a moment after the page first appears.
The home page no longer fetches your home screen dashboard settings and company branding twice on every load.
Fixed the "your home screen dashboard is no longer available" notice never actually appearing when the dashboard you had chosen was deleted.

Added database indexes for the training assignment list (per user), the automation execution log (newest-first and per rule) and the song BPM backfill sweep, so those screens stay fast as the tables grow.
Automation rule execution history is now kept for 90 days (configurable via Automation:ExecutionLog:RetentionDays) instead of forever.

Opening a course, an assignment or a projection program now loads its sections, questions, attempts and parameters with separate queries instead of one multiplied result set that repeated the course text for every combination of rows.
The recurring-training and due-soon reminder sweeps now ask the database for exactly the assignments that qualify instead of loading every assignment for every course and filtering in memory.
Training analytics rankings (top scores, fastest completions) are computed in the database and return only the top rows.
Dashboard pickers (home screen settings, program flow, dashboard list) no longer load every widget of every dashboard just to show names.
User lists used for name lookups and the "is this the first user?" check no longer load and track every account row.
Automation actions checking whether a kiosk is online now run a single existence query instead of loading every connected kiosk.

The Music page's song list no longer redraws every row every second while a song is playing. With a large playlist this made the page sluggish; the list now only redraws when the songs, the selected kiosk or the playing track actually change.
Opening the Music page now loads playlist names plus the songs of the first playlist only, rather than every song of every playlist twice.
Playlist pickers (Music page, playlist widget, automation rule dialog) load names only.
The current user's profile and location are looked up once per browser session instead of separately by the layout, footer, navigation menu, greeting card and page on every load.

Fixed: choosing the 24-hour time format on your account page changed the date/time format for every other user until someone else loaded a page. The preference is now stored in a browser cookie set at login and applied per user; the app defaults to UK format.
Changing the time-format preference now takes effect immediately (the page reloads once) instead of on the next page someone happens to open.

Fixed: the laser-game status widget counted down the shared game timer itself, so with several dashboards open the remaining time dropped several seconds per second for everyone. Each widget now works out the remaining time from the kiosk's last report.
Laser-game status and scoreboard widgets now redraw at most about ten times a second during a game instead of once for every hit.
The digital clock widget in millisecond mode updates ten times a second instead of twenty, and no longer restarts its timer every time the dashboard redraws.
The Clients page no longer re-sorts and reloads its grid every second while it counts up "last seen" times.
The Automation page, the automation rule status widget and the kiosk page now load their independent data in parallel.
Song BPM analysis no longer queues the same song several times while a backlog is being processed.
Kiosk song-cache reports now look up all song names with one query instead of one per cached song.
Removed two unused script libraries (Bootstrap's JavaScript bundle and an input-mask library) from every page load.
Projection program steps now hold for exactly their configured time, including when a program is paused and resumed part-way through a step. Each step used to run a few percent long.
Kiosks with a large song cache no longer risk being disconnected when they report their cached songs: the server now accepts larger kiosk messages.
The server no longer writes every SQL statement to the log, which was the single largest source of log volume in production.
Removed the "Lanyard" text heading from the top of every email sent by the app.
Emails now show the company's logo at the top when one has been uploaded, and the Lanyard logo only when the company has no logo of its own.

summary: Started the new Staff Scheduling system: positions, contract requirements, clock-in PINs and rota settings.
details: Added a Positions catalog under Manage > Rota > Positions, where admins and managers define the jobs staff work (e.g. Customer Service Advisor, Supervisor), each with a colour that will identify it on the rota.
Each staff member's profile (Manage > Users) has a new Rota tab for assigning their positions, choosing a primary position, setting a personal contract override and setting their clock-in PIN.

Added contract requirements (minimum shifts per week, minimum shift length, minimum and maximum hours per week) that can be set as a company default, overridden per position, and overridden again per person - any value left blank inherits from the tier below.

Added a Rota Settings page under Manage > Rota with the holiday year start date (defaults to 6 April), hours in a working day and the shift reminder lead time, ready for the upcoming time-off and rota features.
Staff can set or change their own clock-in PIN from Account Management, ready for the upcoming clock-in terminal.

summary: Added the Rota Builder for planning and publishing shifts, and a My Shifts page for staff.
details: Added a Rota Builder under Manage > Rota where managers plan shifts for their location a week or a whole month at a time, with each shift colour-coded by position.

Shifts start as drafts that only managers can see. Publishing makes them visible to staff, and only the shifts that were added, changed or removed since the last publish count as changes - so a last-minute tweak can be published on its own.

Each staff member's weekly hours are shown next to their name, and a warning appears when a week doesn't meet their contract (for example, fewer than one shift of two hours or more). Hours worked at other locations in the same company count towards the week.
Shifts can't overlap another shift the same person has at any location, and shifts that run past midnight are supported.
Added "Copy last week" (and "Copy from 4 weeks earlier" in the month view) to fill a rota from a previous one as drafts, skipping anyone who already has a shift at that time.
On a phone the Rota Builder switches to a day-by-day list with a day picker.
Added a My Shifts page (and a Shifts button on the phone navigation bar) where staff see their published shifts for the next six weeks.
Removed the old placeholder Clock In page and the sample shift cards on the home page, which showed made-up data. Clocking in returns with the new clock-in terminal.
Deleting a user now keeps their past shift history for payroll records under an anonymous placeholder, and cancels any future shifts they had.

summary: Added clock-in terminals, QR clock-in from your phone, and timesheets.
details: A tablet at the venue can now be paired as a clock-in terminal under Manage > Rota > Clock-In Terminals. It shows who's on the rota today, by first name and surname initial; staff tap their name and enter their PIN to clock in or out.

Staff who forget their PIN, or haven't set one, can scan the code shown on the terminal with their phone instead, signing in first if they need to. The code changes every 30 seconds, so it only works for someone standing at the tablet.

Clocking in is only allowed around a published shift at that location - by default from an hour before it starts until an hour after it ends. The window can be changed under Rota Settings. Clocking out is always allowed.
Five wrong PINs lock that person out on every terminal for 30 seconds, and each further lockout lasts twice as long, up to an hour. Entering the right PIN resets it.
Managers can unpair a terminal at any time, and it stops working straight away.

Added a Timesheets page under Manage > Rota showing each person's clocked time next to their rota, including late starts, early finishes and shifts nobody clocked in for. Managers can approve time individually or all at once, and add or correct time for cover shifts and forgotten clock-ins.
Time left on the clock for 16 hours is closed automatically and flagged for a manager to check, as is clocking out at a different location from the one you clocked in at.
My Shifts has a new My hours tab showing your clocked time for the last three weeks and whether it's been approved.
Deleting a user keeps their timesheet history for payroll records under an anonymous placeholder, as it already did for shifts.

summary: Added time-off requests, holiday allowances and approvals.
details: Staff can request time off from the new Time off tab on My Shifts (or Time Off in the menu). It shows how much of each allowance is left this holiday year, what's booked and what's waiting for a decision.

While filling in a request you see what it costs in days and hours, and a warning if it takes you over your allowance or you're already on the rota that day. Going over doesn't block the request; your manager decides.

Managers approve or reject requests under Manage > Rota > Time Off Requests, with the person's remaining allowance and who else is off at the same time shown beside each one. A rejection needs a reason, which the person sees. An approval can be withdrawn; if the time off has already started, only the days from tomorrow are cancelled and the days already taken stay recorded. Managers can't approve their own time off - another manager or an admin decides it.
Managers can record time off for someone directly, including past dates, for example when someone calls in sick.
Time-off types (Paid holiday, Unpaid leave and Sickness to start with) are managed under Manage > Rota > Time Off Types. Each type can be paid or unpaid, and can count against an allowance or not.

Allowances are set per holiday year as a company default, per position or for one person, in days or hours - for example 28 days of holiday for everyone, 30 for Managers, and unlimited unpaid leave for Customer Service Advisors. The holiday year starts on 6 April unless changed in Rota Settings.

Approved and requested time off now appears on the Rota Builder beside that person's shifts. Scheduling someone on a day they're off shows a warning, and nobody gets a "not enough shifts" warning for a week they're off entirely.

Managers now see a badge with the number of time-off requests waiting for them next to Time Off Requests in the menu, and on the Rota heading so it shows even when that group is collapsed. It updates as soon as someone asks for, cancels or gets a decision on time off - no refresh needed.

Section headings on several pages and dialogs (including Onboarding, Staff Document Types, Roles, the What's New dialog, and the music and projection dialogs) show as headings again instead of plain text.

summary: Added rota and time-off emails, shift reminders, and three new dashboard widgets.
details: Publishing the rota now emails each person affected, listing only their own new, changed and removed shifts - so a last-minute change reaches just the people it touches.

Staff get a reminder email before each shift. It goes out 24 hours ahead by default; the lead time, and a switch to turn reminders off, are in Rota Settings. A shift published at short notice isn't reminded twice.
Managers get an email when someone at their location asks for time off, with a link straight to the request.
Staff get an email when their time off is approved, rejected, withdrawn, cut short or recorded for them, including the manager's reason.
New My Shifts dashboard widget: your next shifts, and your time off, for the days ahead you choose.

New Who's On Today widget: everyone on the rota at a location today, who's on now, later or finished, and whether they've clocked in. It updates as people clock in. On a signed-out kiosk screen it only appears if a location is picked in its settings, and then shows first names only.
New Time Off to Approve widget for managers, listing requests waiting at their location and updating live.
